newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Feb 19.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.
LONDON - UK's leading blue chip index scaled to a fresh record peak as investors shrugged off a pullback on Wall Street and a jump in UK retail sales that points to a rate hike.
The FTSE 100 index added 25.1 points to close at 4,357.4.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade sharply lower, tracking Tuesday's post-bourse slide in electronic trade as the dollar slipped off 34-month highs, the market was seen stable and serious correction not yet in sight. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,233.75, down 42.41 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,209.04.
PARIS - French shares ended lower on profit-taking as investors feared a correction with the market at such high levels.
The blue-chip CAC 40 index finished down 22.76 points or 0.87 percent to 2,594.76.

ZURICH - After a brief consolidation the day before, Swiss shares regained power and posted another record close despite late profit taking that triggered a slide from the day's high, the market was nervous and trade was heavily influenced by hedging transactions, which put SMI futures and several stocks such as Nestle and UBS under pressure.
The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 16.97 points or 0.59 percent to 2,870.95.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock markets key index finished higher after directionless trade for most of the day, the market was now focusing on chemical and steel shares, due to expected solid earnings, but some major blue-chip issues, which had bolstered the market recently, were hurt by profit-taking.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average gained 128.37 points or 0.69 percent to close at 18,599.12.

HONG KONG - Cautious sentiment left Hong Kong stocks flat by the close, with concerns about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and continued unwinding of overweight positions keeping prices in check.
The Hang Seng Index closed 3.38 points or 0.03 percent higher at 13,106.32.
SYDNEY - Australian shares closed lower despite an early record high as futures-linked selling slashed the leaders in the afternoon session.
The All Ordinaries index lost 10.7 points to 2,491.0 after peaking at 2,508.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares closed at a new record high as underlying positive market sentiment overcame early jitters about a weaker rand which put a dampener on industrials. The Overall index added 13.5 points to close at 7,107.7, a new all time peak for the second day running. The Industrial index crept up 1.1 points to 8,369.2 while Golds jumped 32.8 points to 1,481.6.
